title: Erdős #1004 OQ-04: Concrete Witnesses for Distinct Totient Runs
description: Proves concrete witnesses for distinct totient runs of lengths 3,5,7,9,10 and universal existence for all K. Inherits 3 axioms from Erdos1004Problem. 11 theorems, 0 sorries, 3 inherited axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős #1004: for any c > 0, do there exist runs of K = ⌊(log x)^c⌋ consecutive integers with distinct totient values? Conditional on probabilistic estimates from Erdős-Pomerance-Sárközy.
overview.problemStatement: Verify concrete witnesses for distinct totient runs of lengths 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, and prove universal existence for all K.
overview.proofStrategy: Direct computation: for K=3, n=4: φ(5)=4, φ(6)=2, φ(7)=6 — all distinct. Similarly for K=5,7,9,10. Universal existence via axiomatized Erdős-Pomerance-Sárközy result.
keyInsights: **Concrete witnesses**: consecutive runs starting at n=4, 10, 16, 46, 45 witness distinct totient runs of lengths 3, 5, 7, 9, 10.
**Primes give large totients**: prime p has φ(p) = p-1, and consecutive primes have different totients. This gives 'local distinctness'.
**Universal existence**: for large K, the probabilistic argument shows dense concentration of prime clusters forces distinct-totient runs of any length.

conclusion.summary: 11 theorems, 0 sorries, 3 inherited axioms. Distinct totient runs proved with explicit witnesses.
conclusion.implications: The concrete witnesses provide evidence that distinct totient runs of any length exist, supporting Erdős's conjecture about run lengths.
openQuestions: Can the probabilistic argument from Erdős-Pomerance-Sárközy be formalized?
Can the bound K = Ω((log x)^c) be improved?
